stories.headline: Israeli leader Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of racist campaign against Arab citizens
stories.summary: Prominent Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot publicly condemned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for a campaign he says marginalizes Arab Israelis by linking them to Hamas. The criticism underscores internal political tensions over the treatment and rights of Israel’s Arab minority.
stories.inside: Arab Israelis feel targeted by rhetoric that ties them to Hamas, raising concerns about discrimination, political marginalisation and potential impacts on their civil rights.
stories.beyond: The accusations could heighten tensions between Israel and neighboring Arab states and influence the broader Israeli‑Palestinian conflict.

stories.headline: FAA issues nationwide ground stop for U.S. flights due to communication problem
stories.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration halted thousands of flights across the United States after a communication issue disrupted operations. The agency is investigating the cause while airlines cancel or delay nearly 7,000 flights, affecting both domestic and international travelers.
stories.inside: U.S. passengers face widespread delays, cancellations, and uncertainty as flights are grounded nationwide, impacting travel plans and causing economic disruption for airlines and related businesses.
stories.beyond: International flights are delayed or canceled, affecting travelers and airlines in other countries and potentially straining cross‑border travel and commerce.

stories.headline: FAA imposes nationwide ground stop in the United States due to communications outage, halting thousands of flights
stories.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration halted all departures at U.S. airports after a communications outage, delaying or canceling more than 11,000 flights. The disruption affected both domestic and international travel, with authorities seeing no evidence of a security breach.
stories.inside: U.S. travelers were stranded or faced significant delays as flights were grounded nationwide, impacting personal plans and business travel.
stories.beyond: International passengers and airlines experienced cancellations and delays, creating ripple effects on global air traffic and airline schedules.

stories.headline: UN Security Council meets as Iran's near‑closure of the Strait of Hormuz raises global shipping threats
stories.summary: The UN Security Council convened at Bahrain's request to discuss rising attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has effectively shut the waterway that carries about one‑fifth of the world’s oil. The meeting underscores lingering regional tensions after Israeli and US strikes on Iran and the risk of a broader conflict that could disrupt global oil supplies.
stories.inside: Iran and neighboring Gulf states face disrupted oil exports, heightened risk to commercial vessels, and economic fallout from a near‑closed strait.
stories.beyond: The restriction threatens worldwide oil supply, pushes up energy prices, and could draw major powers into the dispute, affecting economies and energy security globally.

sources.title: Security Council LIVE: Fragile Gulf calm tested as threats to Hormuz shipping mount

stories.headline: COP31 underscores climate‑finance shortfall and urges polluters to fund adaptation
stories.summary: UN Secretary‑General António Guterres warned that even a three‑fold increase in adaptation funding would cover less than a third of the needs of vulnerable nations. Delegates at COP31 pressed wealthy countries and major polluters to step up financing, highlighting a large gap between pledged money and required support.
stories.inside: People in vulnerable and low‑income countries risk lacking the resources needed to adapt to climate impacts, threatening lives, livelihoods and infrastructure.
stories.beyond: Rich countries and large polluting corporations face growing diplomatic and financial pressure to increase contributions, influencing international budget allocations and climate‑policy negotiations.

sources.name: UN News
sources.title: COP31: Climate finance falls short as calls grow for polluters to pay

stories.headline: Iran claims it struck US radar in Bahrain in retaliation for US airstrike
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it destroyed a US early‑warning radar in Bahrain as retaliation for a US strike on a communications tower in the Strait of Hormuz. The United States reported intercepting the attack, and the incident heightens regional tensions over the strategic waterway.
stories.inside: The attack puts US personnel and infrastructure in Bahrain at risk and signals Iran's willingness to engage directly with US forces, affecting Iranian public perception of its military strength.
stories.beyond: The strike escalates Iran‑US tensions and could disrupt oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, impacting global energy markets and neighboring Gulf countries.

stories.headline: UN urges rapid delivery of winter aid to Gaza amid deadly rains
stories.summary: The United Nations and partner agencies issued an urgent appeal for winter humanitarian supplies to be allowed into the Gaza Strip after deadly rainfall caused casualties and damage. They warned that lives are at stake and called for swift entry of food, water, medical and shelter aid.
stories.inside: Residents of Gaza need immediate food, water, medical care and shelter as the recent rains have caused deaths, injuries and infrastructure damage.
stories.beyond: The humanitarian crisis adds pressure on neighboring Israel and Egypt, potentially affecting regional stability and prompting international diplomatic responses.

sources.name: UN News
sources.title: ‘Lives are at stake’: Humanitarians call for swift entry of winter supplies in Gaza

stories.headline: UN launches initiative to ensure reliable climate information from AI
stories.summary: The United Nations announced new guidance under COP31 to help people obtain trustworthy climate‑change data from artificial intelligence and to understand AI’s environmental impact. The effort aims to improve the quality of climate information worldwide.
stories.inside: People worldwide will receive clearer, more reliable climate data through AI tools, helping them make informed personal and community decisions about adaptation and mitigation.
stories.beyond: The guidance supports international cooperation by standardising climate‑information practices, aiding governments and organizations across borders in their climate strategies.

sources.name: UN News
sources.title: COP31: New initiative targets AI and reliable climate change information

stories.headline: Armed attacks hinder Ebola response in DRC, worsening outbreak
stories.summary: The United Nations says the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is expanding as armed groups repeatedly target civilians and frontline health workers, blocking containment measures. The violence endangers thousands of Congolese and raises the risk of the disease spreading to neighboring states.
stories.inside: Congolese communities face a higher chance of infection and reduced access to medical care as health workers are attacked and health facilities are disrupted.
stories.beyond: The outbreak threatens neighboring countries, which could see cross‑border transmission and must allocate resources to prevent spread, while regional stability is undermined by the ongoing conflict.

sources.name: UN News
sources.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak: Unrest fuelled by armed groups holds back response

stories.headline: UN launches platform to mobilize $3 bn for climate disaster risk financing
stories.summary: UN agencies unveiled a joint platform at COP31 to secure more than $3 billion in risk financing, aiming to protect 75 million people and their livelihoods from climate‑related shocks and natural hazards by 2030. The initiative seeks to provide pre‑disaster funding mechanisms that can be deployed quickly across vulnerable regions.
stories.inside: People in climate‑vulnerable countries will gain access to pre‑disaster financing, helping safeguard their livelihoods and reduce the impact of extreme weather events.
stories.beyond: The platform will shape international climate‑finance flows, influencing donor countries, global financial markets, and multilateral climate agreements.

sources.name: UN News
sources.title: New platform aims to get money moving before disaster strikes

stories.headline: US officials meet Putin and Zelenskyy after Abu Dhabi talks, agree prisoner swap and plan European involvement
stories.summary: U.S. envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow following Abu Dhabi peace talks that produced a Russia‑Ukraine prisoner‑exchange agreement. The meetings set the stage for further negotiations, including the prospect of European participation in the next round of talks.
stories.inside: Ukrainians could see the release of captured soldiers and civilians, easing personal suffering and raising hopes for a broader de‑escalation of the war.
stories.beyond: The talks involve the United States and Europe, influencing NATO strategy, EU security policy, and the overall geopolitical balance between Russia and the West.

stories.headline: Global Microsoft outage disrupts email, collaboration tools in 74 countries
stories.summary: Microsoft’s Outlook, Teams and Copilot services suffered a widespread outage affecting users in 74 countries. The disruption halted email, online meetings and school communications for businesses, governments and educational institutions, and the company attributes the issue to elevated infrastructure loads.
stories.inside: People in the affected nations lost access to email, online meetings and school platforms, interrupting daily work, education and government communications.
stories.beyond: The outage hampered international business and cross‑border collaboration, delaying communications and transactions that rely on Microsoft’s cloud services worldwide.

stories.headline: Israeli airstrike hits Gaza's Nasser Hospital, killing six and injuring dozens
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike struck the Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, Gaza, killing six people—including a surgeon—and wounding around 28 others. The attack caused extensive damage to one of the few remaining medical facilities in the enclave, worsening the humanitarian crisis.
stories.inside: Gaza residents lost six lives and dozens were injured, and the hospital's ability to treat patients has been severely compromised.
stories.beyond: The strike escalates tensions between Israel and the broader Arab world, drawing international condemnation and raising the risk of wider regional conflict.

stories.headline: Microsoft works to restore global Outlook and Teams outage affecting businesses and public services
stories.summary: Microsoft is scrambling to fix a widespread outage that has taken down Outlook, Teams and other services for users worldwide. The disruption has impacted hospitals, schools, police forces and many businesses, though the company says there is no evidence of a cyber‑attack.
stories.inside: In the UK the outage halted email for hospitals, general practitioners, schools and police, forcing staff to rely on alternative communication methods and delaying routine operations.
stories.beyond: The outage affected millions of users in other countries, interrupting corporate communications, remote work and online collaboration across the globe.

stories.headline: WFP chief warns funding cuts deepen hunger crisis for millions in Sudan
stories.summary: The new Executive Director of the World Food Programme says that reduced funding is worsening the hunger emergency in Sudan after visiting displaced families. Millions of Sudanese face severe food insecurity and rely on aid as the crisis deepens.
stories.inside: Sudanese families, especially those displaced by conflict, are experiencing worsening food shortages and heightened risk of starvation without increased aid.
stories.beyond: The deteriorating humanitarian situation could trigger larger refugee flows and regional instability, affecting neighboring countries and international aid commitments.

sources.name: UN News
sources.title: Aid is the ‘only hope’ for millions in Sudan, WFP chief warns, as funding cuts deepen hunger crisis

stories.headline: World leaders at COP31 focus on cities and climate impacts amid activist pressure
stories.summary: At COP31, UN officials highlighted the human cost of climate change, from flooded homes to melting Himalayan glaciers, and urged action to protect cities and vulnerable communities. Activists pressed governments for stronger commitments, while leaders discussed policies to address urban climate risks.
stories.inside: Communities worldwide are experiencing flooding, glacier melt and other climate‑related hazards that were emphasized at the summit.
stories.beyond: Decisions taken at COP31 will influence climate policies, financing and adaptation measures in many nations, shaping emissions trajectories and city resilience across borders.

sources.name: UN News
sources.title: COP31: Cities rise up the climate agenda as leaders face demands for action

stories.headline: UN report says over 1,000 killed in Haiti in third quarter amid gang violence
stories.summary: A United Nations human‑rights report says more than 1,000 people were killed in Haiti between July and September as armed gangs continue to terrorise Port‑au‑Prince and other areas. The killings highlight a deepening security and humanitarian crisis on the island.
stories.inside: Haitians are living under constant threat from armed gangs, with thousands killed and many more displaced, disrupting daily life and basic services.
stories.beyond: The violence risks spilling over borders, prompting refugee flows to the Dominican Republic and raising regional security concerns.

sources.name: UN News
sources.title: Haiti: More than 1,000 killed between July and September, UN report reveals
